title: When Reusable Temporal Skills Become Causal Bottlenecks

objections.r11_closure: Novelty is procedure-bottleneck identification; skill attribution, reusable-skill learning, and temporal retrieval are explicitly conceded as prior art. No skill-container superiority is claimed.
The false-positive case is foregrounded and the existing zero-call audit preserves equal forced helper execution, condition-position diagnostics, and prompt-length diagnostics.
objections.evidence: targeted/generic 442/442 forced once; no-skill 0/442; condition-position p>.65; targeted prompts 18.85 input tokens shorter on average

objections.r11_closure: The ISO-date audit remains a reproducibility/sensitivity diagnostic and is not promoted into a new scientific result.
objections.evidence: 88/88 observed T1 serialized ISO-date comparisons agree with parsed-calendar ordering

objections.r11_closure: Not executed. The manuscript states that the matched generic is target-blind but not guaranteed behaviorally neutral; a second neutral generic is a new treatment.
Not executed. Operation value is separated from container comparison; no claim is made that callable skill state beats an equivalent retrieval-side temporal treatment.
Abstract/results/limitations/conclusion restrict the claim to conditional procedure-by-model-by-task regimes; small endpoint cells, ceiling cases, and cross-domain grounding nulls remain visible.
Controlled exposure is explicitly distinguished from endogenous skill selection; the paper estimates forced procedure exposure, not autonomous call propensity.
